title: Zone affinity and staggered failover for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers using Dedicated capacity in multi-zone regions need explicit placement policies that guarantee data residency and predictable throughput while allowing graceful failover. Current behavior routes fleets by region only and sometimes places nodes in zones a customer considered off-limits, causing compliance concerns and noisy failovers that break throughput guarantees.

Goal: Implement zone-affinity and staggered failover controls for regional dedicated fleets so operators can: 
- declare preferred/allowed zones per fleet,
- specify staggered failover windows and max concurrent cross-zone failovers,
- preserve throughput guarantees (reserved capacity) during planned and unplanned zone degradation,
- avoid routing traffic to disallowed zones to meet residency constraints.

Scope: This ticket covers the API surface, scheduler policy, autoscaler interactions, observability hooks, and rollout plan for the feature. It does not include UI work for the Console (handled by PM-... separate ticket) nor the VPC network plumbing for Private deployments (follow-up ticket planned).
acceptance_criteria: API: New fleet configuration supports allowed_zones (list), preferred_zones (ordered list), and failover_policy {stagger_seconds, max_parallel_failovers}.
Scheduler: Orchestrator honors allowed_zones strictly, never scheduling nodes outside allowed_zones for a fleet.

Failover: On zone outage, scheduler moves traffic in staggered windows respecting max_parallel_failovers and preserves throughput SLOs for at least 70% of reserved capacity during first failover wave.
Autoscaler interaction: Scale-up decisions prefer preferred_zones and respect per-zone capacity quotas; scaling does not place new instances in disallowed zones.
Rollout: Feature can be enabled per-account with opt-in; can be turned off via safe rollback and preserve existing fleets.
Monitoring: New dashboards display zone affinity violations, failover waves, and percent of reserved throughput preserved during incidents.
E2E tests: Integration tests simulate zone failure and assert traffic shift windows and capacity preservation behaviors.
proposed_approach: 1) API: Add fields to fleet spec: allowed_zones (required non-empty), preferred_zones (optional ordered), failover_policy.stagger_seconds (int), failover_policy.max_parallel_failovers (int). 2) Scheduler: Extend placement algorithm to filter candidate nodes by allowed_zones, then rank by preferred_zones and free capacity. 3) Failover controller: introduce FailoverWave controller that drains and shifts traffic in waves, updating routing table entries with TTLs so in-flight requests are preserved. 4) Autoscaler: respect allowed_zones in scale-up planner; fallback to burst capacity reservations in adjacent allowed zones before creating nodes in a new zone. 5) Observability: emit events for zone affinity breaches, failover wave start/complete, and per-fleet throughput preservation metrics.
design_tradeoffs: Strict allowed_zones vs. soft affinity: Strict ensures compliance but can reduce flexibility and increase throttled capacity during full-zone loss. We chose strict allowed_zones to meet regulatory/residency requirements; soft affinity will be explored as a later opt-in flag.
Staggered failover timing: Longer waves reduce risk of oversubscribe but increase time to recovery. Default stagger_seconds=30 balances speed and risk; customers can tune for their workloads.

Throughput guarantees: Preserving 100% of reserved capacity across sudden zone loss is infeasible without global spare capacity; we aim for >=70% preserved in first wave and auto-burst afterward to recover.
implementation_steps: Design API schema and update proto/json specs (runtime + control plane).
Scheduler changes: implement zone filter and ranking, add unit tests.
Failover controller: implement wave logic and routing updates; add chaos tests.
Autoscaler changes: zone-aware scale planner and reservation logic.
Observability: add metrics, logs, and a small dashboard.
E2E: integration tests in staging with simulated zone outages.
Docs & Console: produce API docs and hand off Console requirements to PM/UI.
Rollout & opt-in: feature flag behind account-level opt-in; staged rollout across pilot customers.
risks: Customers with small regional reservations may observe significant throughput degradation if multiple preferred zones are lost simultaneously.
Incorrect allowed_zones configuration could lead to no valid placement and cause fleet failures; need strong validation and helpful errors.
Race conditions between autoscaler and failover controller during rapid outages could cause transient over-provisioning or throttles.
testing_plan: Unit tests for placement filter/ranker and autoscaler planner. Integration tests that create 3-zone cluster with reserved capacity, then simulate z2 outage and measure traffic shift over time. Chaos run: repeated flaps on zone to validate idempotency. Regression tests to ensure legacy fleets without allowed_zones continue working. Add synthetic SLO tests that assert >=70% throughput preservation in wave-1 for pilot customers.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: fleet.zone_affinity_violations, fleet.failover_wave_{start,complete}, fleet.reserved_throughput_preserved_pct. Alerts: affinity_violation > 0 (P0), reserved_throughput_preserved_pct < 50% for 5m (P1). Dashboards: per-account zone topology, failover history, percent-preserved heatmap.
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal canary on infra fleets; Week 2: opt-in pilot with two enterprise customers (legal/info sec signoff required); Week 3-4: broader opt-in and monitor; Week 6: GA with Console controls after PM/UI follow-up. Rollback: feature-flag off reverts scheduler to region-only placement; failover controller noops. Ensure docs for rollback are in the runbook.
